questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: High academic level and an available research project to gain more practical experience in my field. Also experiencing a different culture and different approach to my field

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university gave quite detailed instructions on what to upon arrival, however due to the amount it was a bit difficult to keep track of what should be done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an entire division to help international exchange students available, to answer questions or help with procedures.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. A lot of sites can easily be browsed to find apartments near campus (~4500DKK/month)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of dorms connected to the university that almost all the other exchange students uses, so if you're social I would recommend going to a dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After being contacted I had to make a huge application with: medical history, relevant classes, grades, future aspirations, fields of interest, an application itself, language score (TOEFL)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was pretty self-explanatory and it was easy to get help because of an available chat with the exchange division.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered to FrontierLab which means that I only had to find a laboratory i wanted to do my project in. I didn't get my first priority but a laboratory based on my field of interest.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offer Japanese courses, which are very fast-paced and require a lot of time and dedication. If you want to focus on the lab I would advise against registereing to japanese classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took the FrontierLab course which does not have a formal level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didn't recieve any lectures or classes since laboratory experience was was more in focus. I think learning to work in a laboratory is very similar across different universities.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Full-time FrontierLab

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend only choosing frontierlab as to have more free-time and depth in your study.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of insurances required which ends up costing a bit. Also the english test score that is required was very expensive!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat is very cheap compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Where I was not really anything. I was located at Suita campus which is less student oriented and there was also Covid

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a professor from another university (Ogura-sensei) that often invites international exchange students to do outdoor activities and is very cheap (~2000 JPY) though you have to be quick to registrate on Facebook. The group is called "Outdoor Adventure Team OGURA"

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Best ramen place in Osaka is called Menya Aozora. Osaka is located in the center of a lot of interesting places. I would recommend going to see Kyoto, Nara and Kobe as it only takes 1 hour to get there and there are more than enough places to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. There are some important things to remember in Japan (Calling by surnames, adding proper suffix when adressing people) but people know you are from abroad an knows you probably struggle with it in the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and show you want to participate

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most students have very poor english skills. So communication on more complicated topics can be difficult. Usually they are better on writing than talking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are very proper and nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Even if it seems that there are a  lot of rules and deadlines you can in many cases talk to them to find an arrangement.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your TOEFL score a good amount of time prior to the application!!! If you are not set on a particular laboratory write an email to the professor and ask them if they usually have exchange students - this makes getting into a lab with other exchange students more easy. You will also need a CESR-document for the visa application which also will take some time to arrive apply for this as soon as you can as to avoid stress regarding the visa.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just enjoying another culture and learning something everyday. Also finishing your own supervised project is rewarding in its own right.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Communication with the other students. And managing time properly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
